key_insight: A new 11,000+ image dataset and transfer learning models, especially VGG16, substantially improved recognition of topological relationships such as touching, overlapping, disjoint, and containment.
clinical_relevance: Better automated topological relationship recognition could support medical image analysis tasks that depend on spatial relationships between structures, such as segmentation review and anatomy interpretation.
method: Built a labeled dataset with 11,000+ images covering key topological classes.
Extracted features using segmentation, contour detection, and grayscale normalization.
Compared classical ML models with deep learning models including VGG16 and InceptionResNetV2.
evidence_signal: VGG16 achieved the strongest result, reaching 89.55% validation accuracy and outperforming traditional classifiers in the reported evaluation.
watch_item: The dataset is newly created and the abstract does not report external validation, so generalizability to other imaging settings may be limited.
paper_title: Exploring Learning Models for Topological Relationship Recognition from Image Data
